name: Ground-Based Equipment Operability (Percent Slope)
description: Classifies a PERCENT-slope raster into six bands of ground-based logging equipment operability, using RAW thresholds at 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 percent: unrestricted ground-based (<= 20), wheeled-equipment limit (20-30, the Oregon OSHA rubber-tired skidder limit), tracked equipment (30-40, the Oregon OSHA limit for crawler tractors, tracked feller bunchers, excavators and loaders), steep-slope equipment (40-50, the Oregon OSHA limit for equipment designed for steep slopes), tethered or high-flotation (50-60, the GMUG forest plan limit for high-flotation equipment and the SBEADMR limit for cut-to-length systems on a slash mat), and cable, aerial or hand only (> 60). The input must be in PERCENT (20% = 11.3 deg, 30% = 16.7, 40% = 21.8, 50% = 26.6, 60% = 31.0); a degree raster would put far too much ground in the gentle classes. These are recurring published values, not a national standard -- duplicate the system and set the thresholds from the forest plan and project decision that govern your area.
source: OAR 437-007-0935(1), quoted in Oregon OSHA's guidelines for tethered logging systems (2016) and the USDA Forest Service Forest Operations Equipment Catalog (Tethered Logging Systems); Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests Land and Resource Management Plan III-41 to III-42, quoted in the SBEADMR Supplemental Information Report on Cut-to-Length and Tethered Logging Technologies (2022).
